summary: All nine occurrences checked. Active I can produce a wound or divide an object completely. Reflexive effects are expressed by a possessed hand/finger or d ruḥe, while the verb remains active; they are not Detransitive solely because actor and possessor co-refer.

Detransitive ṣliḥ is an event of splitting, while ṣliḥo in the existing Part. Pass. describes a split-back state. The glossary's Detransitive terminology is retained. Both impact and m-marked anger can provide causes without an agent phrase.

The wider gloss is a meaning correction grounded in the inherited rock example and new complete divisions, not a stylistic rewrite. No independent new numbered active sense or light-verb phrase is justified.
Existing hand-cut and split-back examples are not duplicated under different PrS numbering schemes; all spellings and inherited references remain unchanged pending source checks.
The one occurrence receives a decision. Round 1 already fills the active Preterit cell to five and broadens sense 1 to splitting/cleaving; its proposals are not repeated.
Ṣləḥ-o-le and ṭəwr-o-le share a feminine patient later identified as šarbo; the digger is the L-agent. This is active stem I, not Detransitive despite the resulting broken object.

The English struck it is less specific than the established cutting/splitting meaning. The following break predicate does not settle whether the first verb entails a complete split or an initial cleaving blow.
The extract is not clearly better than the round-1 body-part and complete-splitting contexts; no new example, generic hit sense, idiom, form or correction is added.
The homonym remains ṣlḥ-1. English is supplied project machine translation; no replacement translation or normalization of source Ṣləḥole is introduced.

summary: In the Detransitive, a personified grain splits from anger (mu qaḥər); this is an expressed cause, not an external agent. A conventional anger idiom is not established by one riddle.

A clay jug is the feminine suffix-resumed patient of an active blow/cut followed by ṭwr break. A nonliving brittle object is compatible with the round-1 split/cleave gloss; no independent generic strike sense is established.
